**Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 76, verse 1:**

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

.

Tafsir of Surat al-Insan

It is Meccan according to some of them.

It is Medinan according to some of them, and it was said: some of it is Meccan and some of it is Medinan.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿Has there come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing worth mentioning?﴾ Its meaning: "There has certainly come upon man a period of time," as al-Farra' said.

It was also said: "There came upon man a period of time." According to the view of most of the exegetes, "man" (al-insan) here is Adam.

On the authority of Ibn Jurayj: it refers to every human being among the children of Adam.

As for His words, exalted is He: ﴿a period of time﴾, it is forty years.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Allah fashioned Adam, peace be upon him, then left him for forty years, looking at him, then breathed the spirit into him.

In another narration: He created him from clay, then after forty years he became dried clay (salsal) without being touched by fire.

In another narration: he was forty years as clay (tin), and forty years as black mud shaped (hama' masnun), and forty years as dried clay (salsal).

As for His words: ﴿he was not a thing worth mentioning﴾, meaning: he was a thing, but not a thing that is mentioned.

It is narrated that this verse was recited in the presence of Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, and he said: "Would that it had been completed," meaning: that state (i.e., of non-existence).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 76, verse 2:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Indeed, We created man from a drop of mingled sperm﴾ mean: mixtures (akhlat).

Ibn Mas'ud said: "Amshajuha" are its veins, which are in the drop (nutfah).

In the language, the word amshaj has the singular mashij, which means mixing (al-khalt).

The meaning is: the mixing of the man's fluid with the woman's fluid, or the mixing of blood with the drop.

It has also been said: Allah the Most High created the natural temperaments (taba'i') that are in man within the drop, from heat, cold, moisture and dryness. These are the amshaj. Then He balanced them, then built the animal structure upon these balanced temperaments, then breathed the spirit into it, then split for it the hearing and the sight. Glory be to Him who created this creation from a despised drop or a foul clot.

It has also been said: amshaj means stages (atwar). The drop is a stage, the clot is a stage, the lump of flesh is a stage, and so on after that.

It has also been said: amshaj means colours (alwan).

In a report: "The man's fluid is white and thick, and the woman's fluid is yellow and thin. When the woman's fluid overcomes the man's fluid, a female is born; and when the man's fluid overcomes the woman's fluid, a male is born."

As for His words: ﴿We shall try him﴾, it means: We test him and examine him.

It has also been said: there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in the verse, and its meaning is: So We made him hearing and [seeing], and We try him and test him.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 76, verse 3:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Indeed, We guided him to the way﴾ mean: the good and the evil. It is like the words of the Most High: ﴿And We guided him to the two highways﴾.

It has also been said: We made clear to him the path of faith and the path of disbelief.

And the words of the Most High: ﴿Either grateful or ungrateful﴾: according to the Basrians, "imma" (either) here has the meaning of "aw" (or). According to the Kufans, its meaning is: "imma kana shakiran wa-imma kana kafuran" (whether he was grateful or whether he was ungrateful).

It has also been said: either wretched or happy.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 76, verse 4:

His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers chains and shackles and a blazing Fire.﴾ It is also read "salasil" (chains). The original form is salasil, which is not declined (diptotic). As for his declining it according to the reading of the one who read "salasila and aghlala and sa'iran" (chains, shackles and a blazing Fire), in agreement with his saying ﴿aghlala﴾ (shackles), this is permissible according to the usage of the Arabs.

Al-aghlal (shackles) is the plural of ghull (shackle).

Jubayr ibn Nufayr narrated from Abu al-Darda', that he said: "Raise your hands to Allah before you are shackled with shackles."

His saying: ﴿sa'iran﴾ means: a fire kindled.

In some reports, with the transmission of 'Atiyya, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: that Allah, may He be exalted, will send a cloud which will stand over the heads of the people of the Fire, and it will be said to them: "What do you want?" They will say: "Drink." So Allah will rain down upon them from it chains, shackles and boiling water.

Al-Hasan said: Indeed Allah does not shackle the disbelievers out of inability to restrain them, but when the Fire subsides from them, their shackles will drag them down to the bottom of the Fire.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 76, verse 5:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed the righteous will drink from a cup﴾. Al-abrar (the righteous): they are the obedient.

It was also said: they are those who were dutiful to their fathers and their sons.

And from al-Hasan: they are those who do not harm an ant.

In some reports: "No child looks at his father with a look of dutifulness and tenderness except that Allah records for him a proof (hujjah) for it." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, even if he looks a hundred times in a day?" He said: "Allah is greater and better."

And His saying: ﴿from a cup﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: the Arabs do not mention the cup (kas) except when wine (khamr) is in it.

The poet said:

(The cup has turned away from us, Umm 'Amr... and the cup used to run to the right hand.)

And His saying: ﴿whose mixture is camphor﴾. That is: it is mixed with camphor, and this is a mixture of scent (wujud al-ra'ihah), not a mixture of taste (wujud al-ta'm).

It was also said: camphor and ginger are the names of two springs (ʿuyun) from the springs of Paradise.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 76, verse 6:

And His saying: ﴿A spring from which the servants of Allah drink⦆ is in the accusative (al-nasb) by way of praise (al-madh), meaning: a spring ﴿from which the servants of Allah drink⦆, i.e., from it, the servants of Allah.

And His saying: ﴿They cause it to gush forth abundantly⦆ means: they make it flow [flowing] as they wish and desire.

It has been said: the verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿAli, al-Zubayr, ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf, Saʿd, and Abu ʿUbayda.

And in some tafsirs: and Ibn Masʿud, Hudhayfa, Salman, and Abu Dharr.

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿They fulfil the vow﴾ means: they fulfil what they have said (their pledges).

It was also said: it is the vow itself.

The first view is the more preferable, because the vow is disliked, as stated in some reports: "The vow is only used to extract [something] from the miser."

The meaning is that the generous person has no need of a vow. In general, fulfilling a vow is praiseworthy.

And His words: ﴿and they fear a Day whose evil is widespread﴾ means: spreading far and wide.

It was also said: extended.

It was also said: scattered.

The poet said:

(And there fell upon the nobles between Lu'ayy ... a fire at al-Buwayra, spreading far and wide)

That is, scattering. The spreading of the evil of the Day of Resurrection is in the heavens and the earth. As for the heavens, it is by the folding up of their sun, the eclipsing of their moon, the scattering of their stars, and the rolling up of the heavens like the rolling up of a scroll, and what resembles that.

As for its evil in the earth, it is by the uprooting of its mountains, the levelling of its rivers, the destruction of its plants, the smashing of some of it upon others, and what resembles that of the transformation of the earth, the destruction of creation, and other things.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 76, verse 8:

And His saying: ﴿And they give food, in spite of love for it, to the needy⁠﻿ ﻿⁠﻿, ﻿﻿⁠﻿⁠﻿...⁠﻿⁠﻿⁠﻿⁠﻿﻿⁠﻿﻿...﻿⁠﻿⁠﻿⁠...⁠﻿⁠﻿⁠﻿

Correction: I must correct my previous rendering, which was garbled. Here is the clean translation:

And His saying: ﴿And they give food, out of love for it, to the needy﴾. That is: out of love for food, and their desire for it and their need of it.

And His saying: ﴿the needy﴾ is the one in need. ﴿The orphan﴾ is the one who has no father. ﴿And the captive﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is the one who is imprisoned or jailed.

It is narrated from Mujahid, Qatadah and a group that it is the captive from among the polytheists.

It is narrated from Abu Sulayman al-Darani: "out of love for God."

There is disagreement about who this verse was revealed concerning. The most correct of the opinions is that the verse is general in application.

The second opinion: it was revealed concerning Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn. This was related by Umar ibn Ubayd from al-Hasan al-Basri, and it is reported from Ibn Abbas in some narrations.

In the story: Ali and Fatimah woke up fasting, and Fatimah prepared three loaves of barley bread, so that she would eat one loaf herself, Ali would eat one, and one would be for al-Hasan and al-Husayn. When evening came, a needy person came and they gave him one of the loaves; then an orphan came and they gave him the second loaf; then a captive came and they gave him the third loaf, and they went hungry.

In another narration: Ali had hired himself out to a Jew to draw water for him in exchange for some barley. That barley was brought to Fatimah, and she made the three loaves from it.

In some narrations: that occurred over three nights.

And God knows best.

In this story there is much confusion, which we have left out of mention.

It was also said: the verse was revealed concerning Abu al-Darda'.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 76, verse 9:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Indeed, we feed you only for the sake of Allah. We wish from you no reward or thanks.﴾ That is: no recompense in deed, and no praise in speech.

It is said in the tafsir (exegesis) that they did not actually utter this statement, but it was in their inner thoughts, so Allah the Most High informed of what was in their inner thoughts.

The Qur'anic verse: ﴿Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day [that is] austere and distressing.﴾

His saying: ﴿Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day [that is] austere and distressing﴾, because faces frown (tanbaʿisu) in it. He attributed the frowning (ʿabus) to the Day in a figurative manner (ʿalā ṭarīq majāz).

The meaning of "we fear from our Lord a Day" is: we fear the punishment of a Day.

His saying: ﴿qamṭarīran﴾ means: severe.

It is said: "a day of qamṭarīr" and "qamāṭir" when the matter in it becomes intense (ishtadda fīhi al-amr).

The poet said:

(O sons of our paternal uncle, do you remember our trials for you, when there was a day of qamāṭir?)

And His saying, ﴿So God protected them from the evil of that Day and gave them radiance and joy﴾: that is, radiance in the face and joy in the hearts.

And nadrah (radiance) is the beauty in faces that comes from blessing, and it is a state of luxury and ease.

And His saying: ﴿And He will reward them for what they endured with a garden and silk﴾ — [that is, for their patience] in obeying the commands and avoiding the prohibitions.

It was also said: [it is for their patience] in trials and hardships, and in hunger together with giving preference to others [over themselves].

And His saying: ﴿a garden and silk﴾ — that is, the gardens and the garments of brocade.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 76, verse 13:

And the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Reclining therein upon couches﴾. Al-arai'k (the couches) are the thrones (al-surur) in the canopied enclosures (al-hajal), upon which are the furnishings (al-furush). The Arabs do not call it arika (a couch) unless it is within a canopied enclosure (hajla).

And the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿They see therein neither sun nor bitter cold﴾. That is: neither heat nor cold.

The poet said:

(A pampered, tender girl, a gazelle... she has not seen sun nor bitter cold.)

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 76, verse 14:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And its shades hanging low over them﴾. "Wa-daniyah" is in the accusative, coordinated (ʿatfan) with His saying: ﴿reclining﴾.

And His saying: ﴿Its shades over them﴾, meaning: the shades of the canopies (al-ḥijāl).

And His saying: ﴿And its fruit-clusters are made low, lowered to them in readiness﴾, meaning: its fruit-clusters were brought near to them.

In the tafsir it is said: when they stood, it rose up to them; when they sat, it descended to them; and when they lay down, it drew close to them. It was also said: nothing prevents them from it, neither distance nor thorns.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 76, verse 15:

And the saying of Allah Most High: ﴿And there will be circulated among them vessels of silver and cups﴾. The *akwab* (cups) are the *abariq* (ewers) which have no spouts; its singular is *kub* (cup).

And the saying of Allah Most High: ﴿They will be crystal-clear glass﴾. Al-Sha'bi said: they will have the clarity of glass and the whiteness of silver.

And from Ibn 'Abbas: that if a piece of silver were taken and made as thin as the wing of a fly, one would not see what was inside it, whereas the silver of Paradise can be seen through from within. Thus, in this sense, it is in the clarity of glass.

And also from him: the glass in this world is originally made of sand, so how could it be, when its origin is silver in Paradise, in beauty and clarity?

And also from him: nothing in Paradise resembles anything in this world; rather, there is only the names in common between what is in this world and what is in Paradise.

"And His saying: ﴿Crystal-clear vessels of silver, which they have determined in measure﴾. That is: measured to the exact amount of quenching thirst, with no excess and no deficiency.

It is also said: according to the size of the palm, that is, according to what it can hold.

It is also said: full."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 76, verse 17:

And His saying: ﴿And they will be given to drink therein a cup﴾ means: from a cup.

And His saying: ﴿whose mixture is ginger﴾. The Arabs used to find the taste of ginger pleasant, so He mentioned it in accordance with what they were accustomed to [to find pleasant].

It was also said: "Zanjabil" is the name of a spring, not that it is ginger known in taste, ﴿and there will circulate among them young boys made eternal﴾. And the fragrance.

Based on this, His saying ﴿whose mixture is ginger﴾ means: its mixture is from the spring of Zanjabil.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 76, verse 18:

And His saying: ﴿A spring therein called Salsabil.﴾ It is said that Salsabil is also the name of the spring of ginger (zanjabil), and it is put in the accusative on the basis of praise (al-madh), and its meaning is: I mean, a spring.

And His saying: ﴿called Salsabil﴾, that is: Salsabil of the flow in their throats.

And in some reports: when it is brought near their mouths, it flows smoothly (tasalsalat) down their throats.

As for whoever said, regarding His saying ﴿Salsabil﴾, "Ask (salni) a way (sabilan) to it," he has gone far astray; that is a false interpretation and is not from the saying of the people of knowledge.

And on the authority of Ibn al-A'rabi, he said: I have not heard "salsabil" except in the Qur'an.

It has also been said: it is the name of the spring, as we have mentioned.

If it is said: when you make Salsabil the name of the spring, how is it inflected (yansarif)? The answer: it is inflected only because it is the end of a verse (ra's aya), and we have explained this before.

Sufyan narrated, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: Salsabil means: very strong in its flow.

Qatadah said: Salsah means: it flows in their throats with the utmost ease.

Tha'lab said: Salsabil means: smooth (layyinan).

And on the authority of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib: Salsabil is a spring that flows beneath the Throne, in a channel of gold.

As for His saying: ﴿whose mixture is ginger﴾, there is another statement, namely that it is mixed for the rest of the people of Paradise, while the ones brought near (al-muqarrabun) drink it pure (sirfan), and it is like the Tasnim, as will come later.

They recited, concerning ginger:

﴿And as if the taste of ginger in it ... when crushed, and the wine's essence﴾

And this indicates that they were able to taste ginger.

It has also been said concerning Salsabil: that it flows over them in their palaces, their upper chambers, and upon their gatherings.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 76, verse 19:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And there will circulate among them young boys made eternal﴾, meaning: youths made eternal.

And His saying: ﴿made eternal﴾, meaning: they do not decay and do not perish.

It has also been said: "made eternal" means adorned with earrings and bracelets (muqarrattun, musawwarun).

The poet said:

(And maidens adorned with silver, as if / their hindquarters were sand-dunes' mounds)

And His saying: ﴿When you see them, you would think them scattered pearls﴾: they are only likened to pearls in clearness, beauty and abundance.

He mentioned "scattered" (manthur) because scattered pearls in a gathering are finer than them strung together (manzum).

In the tafsir of al-Naqqash: they scatter about in service, and therefore He said: ﴿scattered pearls﴾. Had they been a single row, He would have said "strung" (manzum).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 76, verse 20:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when you look, you will see bliss and a great dominion﴾. There is an omission in it, and the meaning is: "When you look at what is there, you will see bliss and a great dominion." Sufyan al-Thawri said: "It has reached us that it is the greeting of the angels upon them."

And it is related from al-Kalbi, Muqatil and others that they said: "It is the angels' seeking permission to greet them, and that is the great dominion."

And in some reports, through the narration of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: "The person of lowest rank among the people of Paradise will have eighty thousand servants and seventy-two wives."

And in some reports also: "For each one of them there are seventy palaces; in each palace seventy houses; in each house seventy chambers; and in each chamber a tent whose height in the sky is one farsakh, and whose width is one farsakh by one farsakh. It has four thousand doors of gold."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 76, verse 21:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Upon them﴾ (ʿāliyahum). It is also read ʿāliyahum (with a fatḥah on the yāʾ). Whoever reads it with a fatḥah on the yāʾ, the meaning is: above them. Whoever reads it with a sukūn on the yāʾ, its meaning is: upon them.

It is said: ʿalayhim, meaning: above them (ʿāl), referring to the canopy (ḥijāl) mentioned before.

And His words: ﴿garments of green silk﴾ (thiyāb sundusin khuḍr), meaning: their colours are green.

Whoever reads it in the nominative (rafʿ), it refers back to the garments (thiyāb). Whoever reads it in the genitive (kasr), it is an attributive adjective (naʿt) of sundus.

Sundus is that which is thin of brocade (dībāj), and istabraq is that which is thick of it.

And His words: ﴿and brocade (istabraq)﴾. It is also read wa-istabraqin. On the nominative reading it refers back to the garments; on the genitive reading it is governed by the preposition, with the implied sense "of brocade" (min istabraq).

And His words: ﴿and they are adorned with bracelets of silver﴾ (wa-ḥullū asāwira min fiḍḍah). Asāwir and aswirah are plurals of siwār (bracelet). If it is asked: what adornment is there in a bracelet, when the wealthy do not care for it? The answer: it has been mentioned elsewhere that they are adorned with gold and with pearls, so they are adorned with gold at times, with silver at times, and with pearls at times, so that it may combine all the beauties of adornment.

It is also said: gold is for women and silver is for men.

It is said: gold surpasses silver only in this world, because silver is abundant and gold is rare; this disparity does not exist in Paradise, and the intent is simply the adornment itself, which exists in both of them together.

And His words: ﴿and their Lord gives them to drink a pure drink﴾ (wa-saqāhum rabbuhum sharāban ṭahūrā). Al-Zajjaj said: it is not impure like the wine of this world.

And from Abū Qilābah and Ibrāhīm that they both said: when the people of Paradise finish eating, they are brought the pure drink, which purifies their insides, makes their bellies lean, and there issues from them belching and perspiration that has the fragrance of musk, so they desire food again.

It is also said: the pure drink is from a spring at the gate of Paradise; when the Muslims drink from it, their insides are purified of every rancour, treachery and envy. This is an opinion, because ṭahūr is the pure, purifying thing, as mentioned in the report.

The evidence for this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ), when he was asked about performing ablution with sea water: "Its water is ṭahūr," meaning: its water is purifying.

Divine words: ﴿Indeed, this has been a reward for you, and your effort has been appreciated.﴾

Al-Shukr (gratitude) when ascribed to the Lord, the Exalted, means accepting good deeds and pardoning misdeeds.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 76, verse 23:

The word of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, it is We who have sent down to you the Qur'an, sent down [in stages]﴾. Its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 76, verse 24:

Regarding His words, ﴿So be patient for the decree of your Lord, and do not obey from among them any sinner or ungrateful one﴾, it is said in the tafsir that the sinner (ātham) is ʿUtba ibn Rabiʿa, and the ungrateful one (kafūr) is al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.

It is also said that the sinner is Abu Jahl.

In some tafsirs: al-Walid ibn al-Mughira said to the Prophet, "What if you were to abandon the religion of your fathers? Perhaps you have only abandoned it because of poverty. Return to the religion of your fathers, and I will give you half of my wealth."

Abu al-Bakhtari ibn Hisham said: "I will marry you to my daughter, who is the most beautiful of women, the most eloquent in speech, and the sweetest in tongue."

Quraysh knew of this.

The Prophet remained silent. Then Abu Mas'ud al-Thaqafi said: "If you fear Allah, then I will grant you protection from Him."

When the Prophet heard that, he stood up and left. Then Allah the Exalted revealed this verse, and His words ﴿Indeed, We have sent down the Qur'an to you, a gradual revelation﴾ up to the end of the two verses.

If it is asked: Why did He not say "ātiman wa-kafūran" (sinful and ungrateful)? And what is the meaning of "aw" (or) here? The answer: the word "aw" here carries an additional meaning not found in "wa" (and), namely the prohibition of obeying each of them individually. For when a man says to another, "Do not obey so-and-so and so-and-so," then if he obeys one of them, he is not fully disobedient. But when he says, "Do not obey so-and-so or so-and-so," then if he obeys either one of them, he is fully disobedient.

This is like their saying: "Sit with al-Hasan or Ibn Sirin," meaning: whichever of them you sit with, you are right; whereas if he says, "Sit with al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin," you will not be right unless you sit with both of them.

Likewise it is said: "Follow Malik or al-Shafiʿi," with this same meaning.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 76, verse 25:

Allah's words: ﴿And remember the name of your Lord morning and evening﴾, i.e., at dawn and at dusk.

And among the odd reports (al-gharib min al-akhbar) is that the Prophet (ﷺ), when he prayed the morning prayer (al-ghadah), would say: "Allahu akbar" three times, and when he prayed the afternoon prayer (al-'asr), he would say: "Allahu akbar" three times.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And during the night, prostrate to Him﴾, meaning: pray to Him.

It was also said: it refers to the Maghrib prayer.

And His words: ﴿and glorify Him through the long night﴾ refer to voluntary prayer from after the final Isha prayer until dawn, and this is by way of recommendation and encouragement (nadb wa istihbab).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 76, verse 27:

The words of the Exalted, ﴿Indeed, these love the immediate (ʿājilah)﴾, mean: indeed, these disbelievers love the immediate, that is, the worldly life (al-dunya).

As for the words of the Exalted, ﴿and leave behind them a heavy day﴾, it is the Day of Resurrection, and their leaving it behind is their abandoning of deeds and striving for it.

As for His words, ﴿heavy﴾, it is permissible that He called it heavy because of the severity of its terror and dread; and it is permissible that He called it heavy because of the decisive judgment rendered in it between the servants and His justice with them, and it is extremely heavy upon them, except for those whom Allah overtakes with His grace.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 76, verse 28:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿We created you and strengthened their make-up﴾. That is: We made their creation strong.

It is also said: We strengthened their joints.

It is also said: it refers to the connecting parts (al-awsal), and He strengthened them with sinews and nerves.

And on the authority of Mujahid: the "asr" (the make-up) is the sphincter (al-shirj), and that is the two muscles of the human being which relax at the time of defecation so that the waste can easily come out; when it has come out, they contract.

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And when We will, We can replace their likes with a complete replacement﴾. That is: We destroy them and create other creatures in their place.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 76, verse 29:

His saying: ﴿Indeed, this is a reminder﴾ means: the verses that We have sent down are a reminder, that is, an admonition and a lesson.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So whoever wills may take to his Lord a way﴾ means: whoever among you, O addressees, wills to take to his Lord a way, it will be made easy for him, since the proofs are present and the excuses are removed, so let him do it.

.

And it has been said: it carries the meaning of a command.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 76, verse 30:

And His saying: ﴿And you do not will except that God wills﴾ returns their will to His will. The meaning is: they do not desire except by the desire of God. This agrees with the creed of the People of the Sunna (Ahl al-Sunna), that no one does anything, chooses it, or wills it except by the will of God.

In some reports: a man used to say: "Whatever God wills and Muhammad wills." The Prophet (ﷺ) heard that and said: "Are you equating (me with God)?" Then he said: "Say: whatever God wills, then whatever Muhammad wills."

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, God is ever Knowing, Wise﴾ has already been explained.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 76, verse 31:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿He admits whom He wills into His mercy﴾ means: into His Paradise. It was also said: into Islam.

The first is better in this context, because Allah the Exalted said right after it: ﴿And for the wrongdoers He has prepared a painful punishment﴾, meaning: the Fire. The word "al-zalimin" (the wrongdoers) is in the accusative because its implied construction is: "and He has prepared for the wrongdoers a painful punishment."

Abu al-Husayn Ibn Faris mentioned in his tafsir, at the end of the surah, on the authority of Jabir al-Ju'fi, from Qays, the freedman of Ali, that al-Hasan and al-Husayn fell seriously ill, so Ali vowed to fast three days, and Fatimah likewise vowed, and al-Hasan and al-Husayn likewise vowed. When Allah the Exalted cured them, they all began the fast. When it was the first day, Fatimah baked three flatbreads of barley and set them before them at their iftar so that they could break their fast. A poor man came and said: "O people of the House of the Messenger of Allah, a poor man is at the door; feed him from what Allah has provided you." 

So they gave him the flatbreads and remained hungry. Then, when it was the second day, Fatimah - may Allah be pleased with her - prepared the same as she had prepared on the first day, and set it before them in the evening so that they could break their fast. An orphan came and made supplication as we have mentioned, so they gave him (their food) and remained hungry.
